who: claude-opus-5-5 (Claude Opus 5.5), L4 piece B (next_solver interner tables), port-memo-1113
where: crates/blaze-memo/src/lib.rs Gid (constructor pub(crate)); every next_solver test that fabricates a def id (ty.rs, region.rs, consts.rs, predicate.rs, persist.rs, interner.rs, interner/tls_cache.rs)
what: Solver unit tests need def ids that name nothing (a FunctionId, a StaticId) to intern a type or round-trip a codec. Under blaze_query they used `FromId::from_id(Id::from_u32(n))`; blaze-memo's Gid has no public constructor, so no test outside blaze-memo can make an id without a whole Memo and an interned struct. Two lanes each guessed a name (`Gid::from_bits`, `Gid::for_test`) and the coordinator then said `from_bits` will not exist.
cost: every fabricated test id written against a guessed constructor; one rewrite when the guess was refused; the first compile will fail at each until L1 names it
cause: blaze-memo hides Gid's constructor (rightly: a persisted word must never hold one), but there is no named, test-only way to make an id in the session arena, so the rule against persisting ids also forbids fabricating them in tests
class: an invariant enforced by hiding a constructor, with no sanctioned test door, so every downstream test invents its own
prevention: blaze-memo gives one test constructor, e.g. `Gid::for_test(local: u32) -> Gid` in ArenaId::SESSION (cfg(any(test, feature = "testing")) or in blaze_memo::testing), and names it in the spec's L1 API section
workaround: all piece-B tests call `blaze_memo::Gid::for_test(n)`, the name tls_cache.rs already used
